clips.send: Lake Maracaibo. A large lake in Venezuela, joined to the Caribbean, sitting on top of one of the world’s biggest oil fields.

clips.send: São Paulo. Brazil’s biggest city and the largest city in the Southern Hemisphere, with about 22 million people in its metro area.

clips.send: Cuba. Cuba won independence from Spain after the Spanish–American War of 1898. In October 1962 American spy planes found Soviet missile sites here, only 90 miles from Florida, and for 13 days the world feared a nuclear war.

clips.send: Canada. The world’s second-largest country by area. Borders the USA to the south; coasts on the Pacific, Arctic and Atlantic oceans. About 90 percent of Canadians live within about 160 km (100 mi) of the US border, where it is warmer and the land is better for farming and trade. Mostly cold with long winters; the far north is tundra and permafrost. Oil (Alberta), timber, fish, wheat, nickel, iron, uranium, fresh water and hydroelectricity. Issues: acid rain, Great Lakes pollution and damage from mining on the Canadian Shield.

clips.send: Canadian Shield. Very old rock scraped bare by Ice Age glaciers, wrapped around Hudson Bay. It has thin soil and countless lakes, but is rich in minerals.

clips.send: Amazon River. The river with the most water on Earth, flowing about 6,400 km east to the Atlantic. Its basin holds the world’s largest rainforest.

clips.send: Mexico City. Capital of Mexico, built on the old Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, 2,240 m up in a mountain valley. About 22 million people live in its metro area.

clips.send: Quebec. Samuel de Champlain founded it in 1608 on cliffs above the St. Lawrence River, and it became the capital of New France. It is the only city north of Mexico that still has its old city walls, and most people there speak French.

clips.send: Great Lakes. Five linked lakes on the US–Canada border — Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario. Together they hold about a fifth of the world’s fresh surface water.

clips.send: 加拿大。世界上面积第二大的国家。南邻美国，濒临太平洋、北冰洋和大西洋。约 百分之90 的加拿大人住在距美国边境约 160 千米的范围内，那里更温暖，也更适合农业和贸易。大部分地区寒冷，冬季漫长；北部是苔原和永久冻土。石油（艾伯塔省）、木材、鱼类、小麦、镍、铁、铀、淡水和水电。环境问题：酸雨、五大湖污染以及加拿大地盾上的采矿破坏。
